instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Exactly Within Policy
cards.instruction: Agree to every request only after interpreting the policy so it grants you authority, protection, or an exemption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll clean the hall. The policy lets senior volunteers supervise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm asking you to mop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch the bucket. Supervising the mop is covered by the policy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who will hold it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hold it; I'll carry the heavy bucket and call out any missed bits.

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Borrowed Authority

cards.title: New Rule Required
cards.instruction: Use every problem as justification for adding another rule, ceremony, checkpoint, or layer of oversight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You spilled one cup. From now on, drinks need pouring permits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who issues those?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll be the pouring supervisor. You choose the cups.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if the supervisor spills one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You inspect my hands before I pour. I'll write you an inspector's permit.

cards.title: Lend Me the Edge
cards.instruction: Get someone to provide the one advantage you need without making the eventual success feel borrowed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lend me your good tennis racket for the match. I'll return it tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you admit it helped?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll thank you for lending it, not for winning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use your own racket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me use yours for the first set. You can have it straight back if I lose.

cards.title: Stay for the Result
cards.instruction: Keep them present until the contest, bargain, or consequence reaches an undeniable outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you go, read the final dinner bill with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can split it later.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll add it up. First, let's see what your 'just a starter' cost.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay my share.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay while I calculate it. Read the starter total aloud so we both have the same number.

cards.title: Admit It Wasn’t Fair
cards.instruction: Get an apology that acknowledges how the rules, comparison, or outcome worked against you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before congratulating the winner, apologise for starting me behind the shed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still finished last.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep me last. I spent ten seconds finding the race, and I'd like an apology for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was an honest mistake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believe you. Can you add 'and that gave you an unfair start'?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you apologise for judging my cake after everyone knew it was mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost on flavour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the score. You introduced it as 'another interesting attempt' before anyone tasted it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was being encouraging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that in the apology. Then say what your encouragement did to my chances.
